items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: I got to tell you this good one about Duke... And, oh, he's a big rugged Irishman... So he came in there... So he gets around to the piano and said, 'Hey, fella, will you play 'Singing in the Rain?''

ctx.x: I got to tell you this good one about Duke. You know, Duke, he's contrary at times, you know, like people would come in and ask him to play a tune and he'll give you that grin, "Yeah. Okay, yeah." So this is at the Cotton Club and this gangster had did time for one of the big bosses there.

And, oh, he's a big rugged Irishman. Bad, real bad. So he came in there and the day they brought him to the Cotton Club they'd got him a big Lincoln limousine, bought him that, gave him money, and got him a little beautiful blond gal. So he came in there -- so he dances like them old Bowery boys, you know. He can't hardly do nothing he's so stiff. You know, and stiff in everything. So he gets around to the piano and said, "Hey, fella, will you play 'Singing in the Rain?'" The Duke, "Yeah, Just's "Singing in the…

Another set come on, no 'Singing in the Rain.' The third set come on, he comes around there and he grabbed Duke by the neck. "I asked you to play 'Singing in the Rain,' God damn it." And so Herman Stark, the manager, had to run up and grab this guy and talk to him and talk him away from Duke. And Herman Stark came back and said, "Duke, are you crazy?" Duke said, "What do you mean crazy?" He said, "He asked me for 'Singing in the Rain.' I'm going to play it." He said, "Yeah, you're going to play it when?" He said,…
